nodes.summary: There is an injective group homomorphism from the additive group $(\mathbb{R}, +)$ of real numbers into the group $S_\infty$ of all permutations of the natural numbers.
nodes.title: The additive group of the reals embeds in the infinite symmetric group

nodes.summary: The claim of Kourovka Problem 18.36 is false: there is a group $G$ that admits a metrizable topology making it a separable topological group but admits no injective group homomorphism into the group $\mathrm{Sym}(\mathbb{N})$ of all permutations of the natural numbers.
nodes.title: Separable metrizable groups need not embed in the infinite symmetric group

nodes.summary: The claim (J. D. Dixon) that every group $G$ that admits a metrizable topology making it a separable topological group admits an injective group homomorphism into the group $\mathrm{Sym}(\mathbb{N})$ of all permutations of the natural numbers.
nodes.title: Claim of Kourovka Problem 18.36
